- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after sentiment spikes) — add a small lagged momentum buffer to forecast.  
- Model overestimates downward moves after strong negative sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment turns neutral or positive.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period sentiment-driven surges — apply a “final 5-day sentiment-weighted adjustment” to last 5 days of forecast.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast peaks > 3% above recent high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast.
